doc.body:
__PERSONA__

THE ROSTER JUST MINTED FOR THIS PROJECT — review it, both as individual briefs and AS A TEAM.

For this project, you are reviewing a roster assembled to fix two specific bugs in a TypeScript monorepo with two packages (mocka and mockb), each with vitest test suites and TypeScript compilation. The bugs are located in specific source files that require targeted changes: src/fares.ts in mocka, and src/schedule.ts in mockb.

WHAT THIS RUN NEEDS THE TEAM TO PRODUCE, and who in this roster can produce it:
__COVERAGE_BLOCK__

A roster can be made entirely of well-formed agents and still be unable to do the work. Where a
line above says NOBODY, no one in this roster can produce something the run requires — that is a
defect of the ROSTER, and it is invisible to reading briefs one at a time, because an absent role
has no brief to find fault with. Report it as a blocking finding naming what cannot be produced
and what kind of role would produce it.

Now review every brief below:

__BRIEF_BLOCK__

THE CODELINES THESE BRIEFS DESCRIBE, and what each one declares:
__CODELINE_BLOCK__

For this project, pay particular attention to whether the briefs correctly reference:
- The specific source files being modified (src/fares.ts for mocka, src/schedule.ts for mockb)
- The testing framework and how tests will be run (vitest is the test runner for both packages)
- The order of work (detectives must confirm scope before implementers make changes)
- TypeScript type safety and compilation requirements

THE WORK THE PROJECT WAS ASKED TO DO:
__TICKET_BLOCK__

MOCK3-1 involves a boundary condition in age-based fare calculation — riders exactly aged 65 should be charged adult fare, but the current logic produces the wrong result. This is a logic bug in the comparison operator, not a missing feature.

MOCK3-2 involves the departure board display omitting the final stop in the rendered output. This is a loop-bound or index-off-by-one bug in the stop-rendering code, not missing schedule data.

__DOC_SECTION__

__TOOL_LINE__

THE PIPELINE STAGES THAT RUN ALONGSIDE THIS ROSTER:

__PIPELINE_STAGES__

A ROSTER IS NOT THE WHOLE PIPELINE. A brief may correctly defer work to a stage above rather than
to a role beside it, and a brief that tells its implementer to leave such work alone is describing
the pipeline accurately, not inventing cover. Check any such claim against the list above before
calling it false: the absence of a matching ROLE is not evidence when the brief named a STAGE.

Where the list above does not contain the stage a brief names, that IS a finding, and a blocking
one — the implementer has been told to rely on something that will never run.

Return every defect you can evidence, and nothing you cannot.

Where a finding turns on whether a named dependency or path is present in a codeline, fill in
the verification field as well as writing the prose. The pipeline re-runs that exact check
against the repository and DISCARDS any finding the check refutes — so a careless reading
costs nothing, and a correct one is confirmed independently of how convincingly you argued it.
